D. AWS DMS continuous replication only.

question: A company runs a critical web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The application currently runs in a single Availability Zone. The business requires that the application remain available even if an entire Availability Zone fails. What changes should the Solutions Architect make?
options: A. Add a second Application Load Balancer in the same AZ.
B. Increase the size of the EC2 instances in the existing AZ so they can handle the full load.
C. Create an Auto Scaling group that spans at least two Availability Zones, register the instances with the Application Load Balancer, and ensure the ALB is configured for multiple AZs.
D. Move the application to AWS Lambda to eliminate the need for Availability Zones.

question: An e-commerce application processes orders asynchronously. During peak sales events the order volume can increase by 20x. The current architecture has the web tier writing orders directly to a relational database, which becomes a bottleneck and causes timeouts. How should the architecture be redesigned for better resilience and scalability?
options: A. Place an Amazon SQS queue between the web tier and the order-processing workers. The web tier enqueues orders; worker instances (or Lambda functions) poll the queue and write to the database. Use an Auto Scaling group for the workers based on queue depth.
B. Add more web servers and keep the synchronous database writes.
C. Increase the size of the database instance and add more read replicas.
D. Replace the relational database with a single Amazon DynamoDB table and keep synchronous writes from the web tier.

question: A company uses Amazon RDS for MySQL as the primary database for a production application. The Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is 5 minutes and the Recovery Point Objective (RPO) is near zero. Which configuration BEST meets these requirements?
options: A. Database running on a single EC2 instance with EBS snapshots every hour.
B. Multi-AZ RDS deployment (synchronous standby in a second AZ) with automated backups.
C. Single-AZ RDS instance with automated backups retained for 7 days.
D. Single-AZ RDS with a read replica in another Region and manual promotion.

question: A global company needs its application to remain available even if an entire AWS Region becomes unavailable. The application consists of a web tier, an application tier, and a database. The RTO is 1 hour. Which disaster recovery strategy is the MOST cost-effective while still meeting the RTO?
options: A. Backup and restore: store daily backups in S3 and rebuild everything from scratch in a new Region when a disaster occurs.
B. Warm standby with a full-scale duplicate environment running in the second Region at all times.
C. Active-active multi-Region deployment with continuous traffic to both Regions.

D. Pilot light: keep a minimal version of the core infrastructure (database replica, AMI, basic networking) running in a second Region and scale out when needed. Use Route 53 health checks and failover routing.

question: A microservices application uses Amazon SQS for inter-service communication. Occasionally a message cannot be processed successfully even after several retries, and the team wants to isolate those messages for later analysis without blocking the main queue. What should be configured?
options: A. Increase the visibility timeout to the maximum value.
B. Configure a dead-letter queue (DLQ) on the main SQS queue and set a maximum receive count. After the threshold is reached, messages are automatically moved to the DLQ.
C. Delete messages that fail processing immediately.
D. Use Amazon SNS instead of SQS.

question: An organization hosts a static website on Amazon S3. They want the website to remain available even if the primary S3 bucket or the Region becomes unavailable. Which architecture provides the highest availability?
options: A. Hosting the website on a single EC2 instance.
B. An S3 bucket behind an Application Load Balancer.
C. Two S3 buckets in different Regions, with Amazon CloudFront configured with origin failover (primary and secondary origins), and Route 53 health checks if needed.
D. A single S3 bucket with versioning enabled.

question: An application runs on Amazon ECS with the Fargate launch type. The service must be able to survive the failure of an Availability Zone. How should the service be configured?
options: A. Disable cross-zone load balancing.

B. Configure the ECS service to use multiple subnets across at least two Availability Zones and set the desired count high enough that tasks can be redistributed if one AZ fails. Use a load balancer that spans the same AZs.
C. Use only the EC2 launch type with a single large instance.
D. Deploy the service in a single AZ and increase the number of tasks.

question: A company has an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. They need to scale read capacity for reporting queries without impacting the primary transactional workload, and they also need automatic failover if the primary instance fails. Which Aurora configuration should be used?
options: A. A single Aurora instance with no replicas.
B. An Aurora DB cluster with a primary instance and at least one Aurora Replica. Use the cluster endpoint for writes and the reader endpoint for reads. Multi-AZ is inherent in the storage layer.
C. Standard RDS MySQL with a single read replica in the same AZ.
D. Two independent Aurora clusters with application-level failover logic only.

question: A cloud architect is designing a system that processes financial transactions. The system must not lose any messages even if a processing component fails, and messages must be processed in the order they were received for each customer. Which Amazon SQS configuration is required?
options: A. FIFO queue with content-based deduplication (or explicit deduplication IDs) and a message group ID based on the customer identifier.
B. Amazon SNS topic with multiple SQS subscribers.
C. Standard queue with a dead-letter queue only.
D. Standard queue with long polling.

question: A company uses Amazon Route 53 to route traffic to an application hosted in two AWS Regions. They want traffic to be directed to the Region with the lowest latency for each user, but if a Region becomes unhealthy, all traffic should fail over to the healthy Region. Which routing policy and feature combination should be used?
options: A. Weighted routing with equal weights and no health checks.
B. Simple routing with no health checks.
C. Geolocation routing only.
D. Latency-based routing with health checks associated with each record set. Route 53 will stop routing to an unhealthy Region.

question: An Auto Scaling group is configured to maintain a minimum of 4 instances across two Availability Zones. During a routine scale-out, some new instances fail the Application Load Balancer health checks because the application takes 3 minutes to start. What should the Solutions Architect configure to prevent the Auto Scaling group from terminating these instances prematurely?
options: A. Set an appropriate health check grace period (for example 180–300 seconds) on the Auto Scaling group so that newly launched instances are not considered unhealthy until the application has finished starting.
B. Increase the desired capacity to 10.
C. Disable ELB health checks and use only EC2 status checks.
D. Reduce the minimum instance count to 2.

question: An organization needs a shared file system that can be mounted concurrently by hundreds of EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones and must remain available if one AZ fails. Which service meets this requirement?
options: A. Amazon EFS (Elastic File System) configured with mount targets in multiple AZs.
B. Amazon S3 mounted via s3fs on each instance.
C. Amazon EBS Multi-Attach volumes.
D. Instance store volumes shared via NFS from one instance.

question: A production application uses Amazon DynamoDB. The team wants the table to remain available even if an entire AWS Region becomes unavailable, with a recovery point objective of a few seconds. Which DynamoDB feature should be enabled?
options: A. On-Demand capacity mode only.
B. DynamoDB global tables with replicas in at least two Regions.
C. Point-in-time recovery (PITR) only.
D. DynamoDB Streams without any cross-Region replication.

question: A company is designing a serverless application using AWS Lambda, Amazon API Gateway, and Amazon DynamoDB. They want the application to degrade gracefully if the DynamoDB table becomes throttled or temporarily unavailable. Which pattern improves resilience?
options: A. Implement retries with exponential backoff and jitter in the Lambda code (or use the AWS SDK built-in retry logic), consider a circuit breaker, and optionally use an SQS queue as a buffer for write operations.
B. Replace DynamoDB with a single EC2-hosted database.
C. Increase the Lambda timeout to 15 minutes and never retry.
D. Make all Lambda functions synchronous and fail immediately on any DynamoDB error.

question: An application currently runs on a single large EC2 instance. The business wants to improve availability and the ability to scale without downtime. Which architecture change provides the greatest improvement in resilience?
options: A. Move the application to a single Lambda function.
B. Add a second instance in the same AZ and use DNS round-robin.

C. Migrate to an Auto Scaling group spanning multiple Availability Zones behind a load balancer, and move session state to an external store such as DynamoDB or ElastiCache if the application is stateful.
D. Increase the instance size to the largest available type.

question: An organization uses Amazon RDS and wants to reduce the recovery time in case of a failure of the primary instance. They also want to offload read-only reporting queries. Which combination should be implemented?
options: A. Two independent single-AZ RDS instances with application-level replication.
B. Amazon Aurora Serverless only, without any replicas.
C. Multi-AZ RDS deployment for automatic failover, plus one or more read replicas (in the same or different AZs/Regions) for reporting workloads.
D. Single-AZ RDS with one read replica in the same AZ.

question: A Solutions Architect must design a solution for processing images uploaded by users. The processing can take several minutes and must not be lost if a worker fails. The system should automatically scale based on the number of pending images. Which architecture is MOST resilient and scalable?
options: A. Users upload images to an EBS volume attached to a single EC2 instance.

B. Users upload images to Amazon S3. S3 event notifications send a message to an SQS queue. An Auto Scaling group of EC2 workers (or Lambda functions) polls the queue, processes the images, and writes results back to S3. Failed messages go to a dead-letter queue.
C. Use a single long-running EC2 instance that polls an S3 bucket every minute.
D. Users upload images directly to an EC2 instance that processes them synchronously.

question: A company has a multi-tier application with a web tier, application tier, and database tier. They want to ensure that a failure in the web tier does not cascade and take down the entire system. Which design principle should be applied?
options: A. Tight coupling between all tiers using synchronous calls with no timeouts.
B. Using a single shared database connection pool without isolation.
C. Loose coupling using message queues (SQS) or pub/sub (SNS/EventBridge) between tiers, health checks, circuit breakers, and independent Auto Scaling for each tier.
D. Placing all tiers on the same EC2 instance.

question: An Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group is used for a stateful application that stores session data on the local disk. When instances are terminated during scale-in, users lose their sessions. How can this be resolved while still using Auto Scaling?
options: A. Use only Spot Instances so that interruptions are expected.
B. Move session state to an external shared store such as Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon ElastiCache, or a shared EFS file system, and configure the Auto Scaling group to use ELB health checks.
C. Disable scale-in completely.
D. Increase the health check grace period to 1 hour.

question: A company needs to ensure that its Amazon Aurora database can survive the failure of an entire Availability Zone with minimal downtime. What is the recommended configuration?
options: A. A single Aurora instance in one AZ.
B. Two separate Aurora clusters in the same AZ with manual failover.
C. An Aurora cluster with the primary instance and at least one replica placed in different Availability Zones. Aurora storage is already replicated across three AZs.
D. Using Amazon RDS for MySQL with a single Multi-AZ standby only, without Aurora.

question: A media company serves video files and static assets to a global audience. Users are complaining about high latency when downloading content. The origin is an S3 bucket in us-east-1. Which solution will MOST improve performance for global users?
options: A. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the S3 bucket as the origin, enable appropriate caching, and optionally use S3 Transfer Acceleration for uploads.
B. Copy the entire bucket to every AWS Region and use Route 53 geolocation routing.
C. Move the bucket to a single Region closer to the majority of users and accept higher latency for others.
D. Increase the S3 bucket storage class to S3 Intelligent-Tiering.

question: An application experiences a sudden 10x increase in read traffic to its Amazon RDS MySQL database during peak hours, causing CPU saturation and slow responses. The write volume remains low and steady. What is the MOST effective way to improve read performance?
options: A. Enable Multi-AZ on the primary instance.
B. Create one or more read replicas and configure the application to send read queries to the replica endpoints (or use a reader endpoint if using Aurora).
C. Change the instance class of the primary to a much larger size.
D. Switch the storage type to magnetic.

question: A high-performance computing (HPC) workload needs to run tightly coupled simulations across dozens of EC2 instances. The instances require extremely low latency and high bandwidth network communication. Which configuration is MOST appropriate?
options: A. Place each instance in a different Availability Zone and use a Network Load Balancer.
B. Use T3 burstable instances with standard networking.
C. Distribute the instances across multiple Regions for higher availability.

D. Launch the instances in a cluster placement group within a single Availability Zone, use an instance type that supports enhanced networking (ENA) and preferably Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA), and select a network-optimized instance family (for example C5n, C6i, or HPC-oriented types).

question: A web application serves personalized content and product recommendations. Response times are currently 800–1200 ms, and the business wants to reduce this to under 200 ms for the majority of users. Database queries are the main bottleneck. Which combination of services is MOST likely to achieve the target?
options: A. Keep the existing architecture and simply increase the RDS instance size.
B. Replace the database with Amazon S3.

C. Introduce Amazon ElastiCache (Redis or Memcached) to cache frequent queries and session data, add CloudFront for static assets, and consider DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) if the data layer moves to DynamoDB.
D. Move the entire application to a single large EC2 instance.

question: An analytics team needs to ingest and process millions of events per second from IoT devices and click streams with low latency. The data must be available for real-time dashboards and also stored for later batch processing. Which AWS service is the BEST fit for the ingestion layer?
options: A. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams (or Amazon MSK if Kafka compatibility is required).
B. Amazon SQS Standard queues.
C. Amazon S3 with multipart uploads only.
D. Amazon SNS with email subscriptions.

question: A company has an Application Load Balancer distributing traffic to EC2 instances. They want to route requests for /api/* to one target group and requests for /static/* to another target group that serves content from a different set of instances (or from S3 via a different architecture). Which ALB feature enables this?
options: A. Path-based routing (and optionally host-based routing) rules on the listener.
B. Network Load Balancer cross-zone load balancing.
C. Classic Load Balancer only.
D. Sticky sessions only.

question: A database workload on Amazon EC2 requires consistent high IOPS (tens of thousands) and low latency for random read/write operations. Which Amazon EBS volume type should be selected?
options: A. Cold HDD (sc1).
B. Throughput Optimized HDD (st1).
C. Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1 or io2 / io2 Block Express) sized for the required IOPS and throughput.
D. General Purpose SSD (gp2) without any provisioned capacity.

question: A mobile gaming company needs to store and retrieve player session data with microsecond latency. The data is simple key-value pairs and is accessed extremely frequently. Which service is the BEST fit?
options: A. Amazon S3 with Transfer Acceleration.
B. Amazon RDS for MySQL with a large instance class.
C. Amazon Glacier Instant Retrieval.
D. Amazon ElastiCache for Redis (or MemoryDB for Redis if durability is also required).

question: Users in Asia and Europe are uploading large media files to an S3 bucket in us-east-1 and experiencing slow upload speeds. Which S3 feature can improve upload performance without requiring the users to change their upload tool significantly?
options: A. Disabling multipart uploads.
B. S3 Transfer Acceleration, which routes uploads through CloudFront edge locations.
C. S3 One Zone-IA.
D. S3 Glacier Deep Archive storage class.

question: An application uses Amazon DynamoDB and is experiencing hot partitions and throttling under heavy write load. The partition key is a low-cardinality attribute (for example status = "active"). What is the MOST effective remediation?
options: A. Switch to eventually consistent reads.
B. Increase the provisioned write capacity units only.

C. Redesign the partition key to have higher cardinality (for example include a random suffix, a timestamp component, or a more unique identifier) so that writes are distributed evenly across partitions. Consider write sharding if necessary.
D. Enable DynamoDB Streams.

question: A company wants to serve both static assets and a dynamic API from the same domain name with low latency worldwide. Which architecture is recommended?
options: A. Amazon S3 static website hosting only.
B. A single EC2 instance in one Region with a public IP.
C. Route 53 latency routing to different ALBs without a CDN.

D. Amazon CloudFront with multiple origins (S3 for static content, API Gateway or ALB for the dynamic API), using cache behaviors to route paths appropriately, and Lambda@Edge or CloudFront Functions if light request manipulation is needed at the edge.

question: A data processing pipeline needs to read a large CSV file stored in S3 and extract only a subset of rows and columns for further processing. Transferring the entire object every time is expensive and slow. Which feature can improve performance and reduce cost?
options: A. Downloading the full object and filtering client-side every time.
B. S3 Select (or S3 Glacier Select for archived objects) to retrieve only the required data using SQL-like expressions.
C. Moving the object to Glacier Deep Archive permanently.
D. Enabling S3 Versioning.

question: An application requires a shared, high-throughput file system that can be accessed concurrently by thousands of EC2 instances for a machine-learning training job. Which storage service is designed for this use case?
options: A. Amazon S3 with the AWS SDK only.
B. Amazon FSx for Lustre, which is optimized for high-performance computing and can be linked to S3 for long-term storage.
C. Amazon EBS gp3 volumes attached to each instance independently.
D. Amazon EFS with the default bursting mode and no performance considerations.

question: An organization observes that their Amazon CloudFront distribution has a low cache hit ratio for dynamic content. What actions can improve the cache hit ratio?
options: A. Use only signed URLs without any caching configuration.
B. Disable caching entirely so that every request goes to the origin.
C. Review and optimize cache keys (query strings, headers, cookies), set appropriate TTLs via Cache-Control headers or CloudFront cache policies, and consider Origin Shield for multi-Region origins.
D. Increase the origin request timeout to the maximum.

question: A real-time bidding application needs to handle hundreds of thousands of requests per second with consistent single-digit millisecond latency. Which load balancer and compute combination is MOST suitable?
options: A. Application Load Balancer with T3 instances.
B. Network Load Balancer (Layer 4) with a fleet of network-optimized EC2 instances or containers, possibly using AWS Global Accelerator for multi-Region entry points.
C. Amazon API Gateway with Lambda only, without any performance testing.
D. Classic Load Balancer with a single large instance.

question: An application uses Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. Reporting queries are slowing down the primary instance. The team wants to isolate analytics workloads without impacting transactional performance. What should they do?
options: A. Add Aurora Replicas and direct reporting queries to the reader endpoint. For heavier analytics, consider Aurora parallel query or exporting data to a data warehouse such as Redshift.
B. Increase the size of the primary instance only.
C. Switch to a single-AZ deployment to reduce latency.
D. Disable Multi-AZ.

question: A company needs to process large amounts of data stored in S3 with Apache Spark. They want a managed service that can scale the compute automatically and is optimized for S3. Which service should they choose?
options: A. Amazon EC2 instances with Spark installed manually.
B. Amazon EMR (with Spark) or AWS Glue for ETL-style workloads, both of which integrate tightly with S3.
C. Amazon Athena only for all Spark jobs.
D. AWS Lambda with 15-minute timeouts for multi-hour Spark jobs.

question: A web application experiences unpredictable traffic spikes that last for only a few minutes. The current Auto Scaling group takes several minutes to launch new instances, so users experience errors during the spike. How can performance during spikes be improved?
options: A. Disable Auto Scaling and use a single very large instance.
B. Increase the minimum capacity of the Auto Scaling group permanently to the peak level.

C. Use a combination of scheduled scaling (if spikes are predictable), target tracking or step scaling policies, and consider warm pools or a serverless front-end (Lambda/API Gateway) for the most spiky components. Also ensure the AMI is optimized for fast boot times.
D. Use only Spot Instances without any On-Demand capacity.

question: An application needs to query large amounts of structured data stored in S3 without managing any infrastructure. Query latency of a few seconds is acceptable. Which service is designed for this?
options: A. Amazon EC2 with a self-managed database.
B. Amazon RDS with the data loaded into a single large instance.
C. Amazon Redshift Spectrum or Amazon Athena (serverless SQL queries directly on S3 data).
D. Amazon DynamoDB with a scan operation on every query.

question: An organization is running a containerized microservices application on Amazon EKS. Some services need to communicate with extremely low latency. Which networking approach is recommended for high performance?
options: A. Use the Amazon VPC CNI plugin (or an alternative high-performance CNI), consider AWS App Mesh or Kubernetes native service discovery, and place latency-sensitive pods in the same Availability Zone when possible. For the highest performance, evaluate VPC Lattice or host-mode networking carefully.
B. Route all service-to-service traffic through a public Application Load Balancer.
C. Use only ClusterIP services with no consideration of AZ placement.
D. Expose every pod with a public IP address.

question: A data lake on S3 is queried frequently by multiple teams using different tools. Some queries scan the same large datasets repeatedly. What can improve performance and reduce cost?
options: A. Disable all indexing and partitioning.

B. Convert data to columnar formats (Parquet/ORC), partition the data by relevant keys (date, region, etc.), use compression, and consider a metadata/catalog layer such as AWS Glue Data Catalog. Caching layers or materialized views in a query engine can also help.
C. Move all data to Amazon Glacier.
D. Keep the data in a single large CSV file and scan it every time.

question: An application uses Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. Under load, some clients experience high latency. The team has already optimized the Lambda code. What additional steps can improve performance?
options: A. Enable API Gateway caching for appropriate GET endpoints, provision concurrency for critical Lambda functions to reduce cold starts, and consider Lambda SnapStart (for Java) or larger memory settings (which also increase CPU).
B. Increase the Lambda timeout to 15 minutes for every function.
C. Disable all caching and force every request to hit Lambda.
D. Replace API Gateway with a single EC2 instance.

question: An organization needs a high-performance, fully managed Windows file share that supports SMB and can be accessed from thousands of EC2 instances and on-premises servers. Which service is the best fit?
options: A. Amazon S3 with a Windows NFS gateway.
B. Amazon FSx for Windows File Server.
C. Amazon EFS (primarily NFS).
D. Amazon EBS volumes shared via Windows DFS without a managed service.

question: A real-time analytics dashboard needs to display metrics with a latency of only a few seconds after the events occur. Events are generated at a high rate. Which pipeline is MOST appropriate?
options: A. Store every event as a separate object in S3 and run Athena queries on every page load.
B. Use Amazon SQS with a visibility timeout of 12 hours.
C. Write events synchronously to an RDS database and query it from the dashboard.

D. Ingest events into Amazon Kinesis Data Streams (or Firehose), process them with Kinesis Data Analytics or Lambda, and write aggregated results to a low-latency store such as DynamoDB or ElastiCache for the dashboard to query.

question: An application is experiencing high latency when reading frequently accessed data from Amazon DynamoDB. The table is already provisioned with sufficient capacity. What can further reduce latency?
options: A. Enable DynamoDB Streams and process every read through a Lambda function.
B. Switch all reads to strongly consistent reads.
C. Add DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX), an in-memory cache cluster that sits in front of DynamoDB and can reduce read latency to microseconds for cache hits.
D. Decrease the provisioned capacity.

question: A company wants to reduce the time it takes for large files to be downloaded by users around the world. The files are stored in S3. In addition to CloudFront, which S3 feature can help with the initial upload of those large files from distributed offices?
options: A. S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval.
B. S3 Object Lock.
C. S3 Inventory.
D. S3 Transfer Acceleration.

question: A machine-learning training job needs access to a large dataset stored in S3. The training instances require very high sequential read throughput. Which combination provides the best performance?
options: A. Mount S3 using a user-space file system (s3fs) on each instance.
B. Use Amazon EFS with the default performance mode.
C. Copy the entire dataset to an EBS volume on one instance and share it via NFS.

D. Use Amazon FSx for Lustre linked to the S3 bucket (or Amazon S3 with the high-performance AWS CRT libraries / S3A connector for Spark), and place the compute instances in a cluster placement group with enhanced networking.

question: An Application Load Balancer is used in front of a fleet of EC2 instances. Some requests are long-running (several minutes). The default idle timeout is causing connections to be closed. How can this be addressed?
options: A. Reduce the number of instances so that each handles fewer requests.
B. Disable the load balancer entirely.
C. Switch to a Network Load Balancer which has no idle timeout configuration.
D. Increase the ALB idle timeout setting to a value that accommodates the longest expected request (up to 4000 seconds).

question: A company is designing a content delivery architecture for software downloads (multi-GB files). They want the highest possible download speeds for users worldwide and the ability to invalidate content quickly when a new version is released. Which combination is recommended?
options: A. Amazon CloudFront with an S3 origin, appropriate cache behaviors, and the ability to create invalidations (or use versioned object keys for cache busting).
B. A single S3 bucket in one Region with public access.
C. Amazon EBS volumes with snapshots shared publicly.
D. AWS Snowball devices shipped to each user.

question: An application needs to perform complex graph queries with millisecond latency on a highly connected dataset. Which purpose-built AWS database service is designed for this workload?
options: A. Amazon DynamoDB with multiple GSIs and application-side joins.
B. Amazon Redshift.
C. Amazon RDS for MySQL with recursive CTEs.
D. Amazon Neptune (graph database).

question: A media company serves video files and static assets to a global audience. Users are complaining about high latency when downloading content. The origin is an S3 bucket in us-east-1. Which solution will MOST improve performance for global users?
options: A. Move the bucket to a single Region closer to the majority of users and accept higher latency for others.
B. Increase the S3 bucket storage class to S3 Intelligent-Tiering.
C. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the S3 bucket as the origin, enable appropriate caching, and optionally use S3 Transfer Acceleration for uploads.
D. Copy the entire bucket to every AWS Region and use Route 53 geolocation routing.

D. Use T3 burstable instances with standard networking.

options: A. Amazon RDS for MySQL with a large instance class.
B. Amazon ElastiCache for Redis (or MemoryDB for Redis if durability is also required).

options: A. S3 Glacier Deep Archive storage class.

B. Application Load Balancer with T3 instances.
C. Network Load Balancer (Layer 4) with a fleet of network-optimized EC2 instances or containers, possibly using AWS Global Accelerator for multi-Region entry points.
D. Classic Load Balancer with a single large instance.

question: An application uses Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. Reporting queries are slowing down the primary instance. The team wants to isolate analytics workloads without impacting transactional performance. What should they do?
options: A. Switch to a single-AZ deployment to reduce latency.
B. Increase the size of the primary instance only.
C. Disable Multi-AZ.
D. Add Aurora Replicas and direct reporting queries to the reader endpoint. For heavier analytics, consider Aurora parallel query or exporting data to a data warehouse such as Redshift.

question: A company needs to process large amounts of data stored in S3 with Apache Spark. They want a managed service that can scale the compute automatically and is optimized for S3. Which service should they choose?
options: A. Amazon EC2 instances with Spark installed manually.
B. AWS Lambda with 15-minute timeouts for multi-hour Spark jobs.
C. Amazon EMR (with Spark) or AWS Glue for ETL-style workloads, both of which integrate tightly with S3.
D. Amazon Athena only for all Spark jobs.

question: A web application experiences unpredictable traffic spikes that last for only a few minutes. The current Auto Scaling group takes several minutes to launch new instances, so users experience errors during the spike. How can performance during spikes be improved?
options: A. Disable Auto Scaling and use a single very large instance.
B. Use only Spot Instances without any On-Demand capacity.

C. Use a combination of scheduled scaling (if spikes are predictable), target tracking or step scaling policies, and consider warm pools or a serverless front-end (Lambda/API Gateway) for the most spiky components. Also ensure the AMI is optimized for fast boot times.
D. Increase the minimum capacity of the Auto Scaling group permanently to the peak level.

question: An application needs to query large amounts of structured data stored in S3 without managing any infrastructure. Query latency of a few seconds is acceptable. Which service is designed for this?
options: A. Amazon DynamoDB with a scan operation on every query.
B. Amazon Redshift Spectrum or Amazon Athena (serverless SQL queries directly on S3 data).
C. Amazon EC2 with a self-managed database.
D. Amazon RDS with the data loaded into a single large instance.

question: An organization is running a containerized microservices application on Amazon EKS. Some services need to communicate with extremely low latency. Which networking approach is recommended for high performance?
options: A. Expose every pod with a public IP address.

B. Use the Amazon VPC CNI plugin (or an alternative high-performance CNI), consider AWS App Mesh or Kubernetes native service discovery, and place latency-sensitive pods in the same Availability Zone when possible. For the highest performance, evaluate VPC Lattice or host-mode networking carefully.
C. Route all service-to-service traffic through a public Application Load Balancer.
D. Use only ClusterIP services with no consideration of AZ placement.

question: A data lake on S3 is queried frequently by multiple teams using different tools. Some queries scan the same large datasets repeatedly. What can improve performance and reduce cost?
options: A. Convert data to columnar formats (Parquet/ORC), partition the data by relevant keys (date, region, etc.), use compression, and consider a metadata/catalog layer such as AWS Glue Data Catalog. Caching layers or materialized views in a query engine can also help.
B. Move all data to Amazon Glacier.
C. Disable all indexing and partitioning.
D. Keep the data in a single large CSV file and scan it every time.

question: An application uses Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. Under load, some clients experience high latency. The team has already optimized the Lambda code. What additional steps can improve performance?
options: A. Disable all caching and force every request to hit Lambda.
B. Increase the Lambda timeout to 15 minutes for every function.

C. Enable API Gateway caching for appropriate GET endpoints, provision concurrency for critical Lambda functions to reduce cold starts, and consider Lambda SnapStart (for Java) or larger memory settings (which also increase CPU).
D. Replace API Gateway with a single EC2 instance.

question: A company needs a high-performance, fully managed Windows file share that supports SMB and can be accessed from thousands of EC2 instances and on-premises servers. Which service is the best fit?
options: A. Amazon S3 with a Windows NFS gateway.
B. Amazon EBS volumes shared via Windows DFS without a managed service.
C. Amazon FSx for Windows File Server.
D. Amazon EFS (primarily NFS).

question: A real-time analytics dashboard needs to display metrics with a latency of only a few seconds after the events occur. Events are generated at a high rate. Which pipeline is MOST appropriate?
options: A. Store every event as a separate object in S3 and run Athena queries on every page load.

B. Ingest events into Amazon Kinesis Data Streams (or Firehose), process them with Kinesis Data Analytics or Lambda, and write aggregated results to a low-latency store such as DynamoDB or ElastiCache for the dashboard to query.
C. Use Amazon SQS with a visibility timeout of 12 hours.
D. Write events synchronously to an RDS database and query it from the dashboard.

question: An application is experiencing high latency when reading frequently accessed data from Amazon DynamoDB. The table is already provisioned with sufficient capacity. What can further reduce latency?
options: A. Switch all reads to strongly consistent reads.
B. Add DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX), an in-memory cache cluster that sits in front of DynamoDB and can reduce read latency to microseconds for cache hits.
C. Enable DynamoDB Streams and process every read through a Lambda function.
D. Decrease the provisioned capacity.

question: An organization wants to reduce the time it takes for large files to be downloaded by users around the world. The files are stored in S3. In addition to CloudFront, which S3 feature can help with the initial upload of those large files from distributed offices?
options: A. S3 Object Lock.
B. S3 Inventory.
C. S3 Transfer Acceleration.
D. S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval.

question: A machine-learning training job needs access to a large dataset stored in S3. The training instances require very high sequential read throughput. Which combination provides the best performance?
options: A. Copy the entire dataset to an EBS volume on one instance and share it via NFS.
B. Mount S3 using a user-space file system (s3fs) on each instance.

C. Use Amazon FSx for Lustre linked to the S3 bucket (or Amazon S3 with the high-performance AWS CRT libraries / S3A connector for Spark), and place the compute instances in a cluster placement group with enhanced networking.
D. Use Amazon EFS with the default performance mode.

question: An Application Load Balancer is used in front of a fleet of EC2 instances. Some requests are long-running (several minutes). The default idle timeout is causing connections to be closed. How can this be addressed?
options: A. Reduce the number of instances so that each handles fewer requests.
B. Switch to a Network Load Balancer which has no idle timeout configuration.
C. Increase the ALB idle timeout setting to a value that accommodates the longest expected request (up to 4000 seconds).
D. Disable the load balancer entirely.

question: An organization is designing a content delivery architecture for software downloads (multi-GB files). They want the highest possible download speeds for users worldwide and the ability to invalidate content quickly when a new version is released. Which combination is recommended?
options: A. Amazon CloudFront with an S3 origin, appropriate cache behaviors, and the ability to create invalidations (or use versioned object keys for cache busting).
B. Amazon EBS volumes with snapshots shared publicly.
C. A single S3 bucket in one Region with public access.
D. AWS Snowball devices shipped to each user.

question: An application needs to perform complex graph queries with millisecond latency on a highly connected dataset. Which purpose-built AWS database service is designed for this workload?
options: A. Amazon Redshift.
B. Amazon RDS for MySQL with recursive CTEs.
C. Amazon Neptune (graph database).
D. Amazon DynamoDB with multiple GSIs and application-side joins.

question: A media company serves video files and static assets to a global audience. Users are complaining about high latency when downloading content. The origin is an S3 bucket in us-east-1. Which solution will MOST improve performance for global users?
options: A. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the S3 bucket as the origin, enable appropriate caching, and optionally use S3 Transfer Acceleration for uploads.
B. Increase the S3 bucket storage class to S3 Intelligent-Tiering.
C. Copy the entire bucket to every AWS Region and use Route 53 geolocation routing.
D. Move the bucket to a single Region closer to the majority of users and accept higher latency for others.

question: An application experiences a sudden 10x increase in read traffic to its Amazon RDS MySQL database during peak hours, causing CPU saturation and slow responses. The write volume remains low and steady. What is the MOST effective way to improve read performance?
options: A. Create one or more read replicas and configure the application to send read queries to the replica endpoints (or use a reader endpoint if using Aurora).
B. Enable Multi-AZ on the primary instance.
C. Switch the storage type to magnetic.
D. Change the instance class of the primary to a much larger size.

question: A high-performance computing (HPC) workload needs to run tightly coupled simulations across dozens of EC2 instances. The instances require extremely low latency and high bandwidth network communication. Which configuration is MOST appropriate?
options: A. Use T3 burstable instances with standard networking.

B. Launch the instances in a cluster placement group within a single Availability Zone, use an instance type that supports enhanced networking (ENA) and preferably Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA), and select a network-optimized instance family (for example C5n, C6i, or HPC-oriented types).
C. Distribute the instances across multiple Regions for higher availability.
D. Place each instance in a different Availability Zone and use a Network Load Balancer.

question: A web application serves personalized content and product recommendations. Response times are currently 800–1200 ms, and the business wants to reduce this to under 200 ms for the majority of users. Database queries are the main bottleneck. Which combination of services is MOST likely to achieve the target?
options: A. Keep the existing architecture and simply increase the RDS instance size.
B. Replace the database with Amazon S3.
C. Move the entire application to a single large EC2 instance.

D. Introduce Amazon ElastiCache (Redis or Memcached) to cache frequent queries and session data, add CloudFront for static assets, and consider DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) if the data layer moves to DynamoDB.

question: An analytics team needs to ingest and process millions of events per second from IoT devices and click streams with low latency. The data must be available for real-time dashboards and also stored for later batch processing. Which AWS service is the BEST fit for the ingestion layer?
options: A. Amazon SNS with email subscriptions.
B. Amazon S3 with multipart uploads only.
C. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams (or Amazon MSK if Kafka compatibility is required).
D. Amazon SQS Standard queues.

question: A company has an Application Load Balancer distributing traffic to EC2 instances. They want to route requests for /api/* to one target group and requests for /static/* to another target group that serves content from a different set of instances (or from S3 via a different architecture). Which ALB feature enables this?
options: A. Path-based routing (and optionally host-based routing) rules on the listener.
B. Sticky sessions only.
C. Classic Load Balancer only.
D. Network Load Balancer cross-zone load balancing.

question: A database workload on Amazon EC2 requires consistent high IOPS (tens of thousands) and low latency for random read/write operations. Which Amazon EBS volume type should be selected?
options: A. Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1 or io2 / io2 Block Express) sized for the required IOPS and throughput.
B. Cold HDD (sc1).
C. Throughput Optimized HDD (st1).
D. General Purpose SSD (gp2) without any provisioned capacity.

question: A mobile gaming company needs to store and retrieve player session data with microsecond latency. The data is simple key-value pairs and is accessed extremely frequently. Which service is the BEST fit?
options: A. Amazon S3 with Transfer Acceleration.
B. Amazon Glacier Instant Retrieval.
C. Amazon ElastiCache for Redis (or MemoryDB for Redis if durability is also required).
D. Amazon RDS for MySQL with a large instance class.

question: Users in Asia and Europe are uploading large media files to an S3 bucket in us-east-1 and experiencing slow upload speeds. Which S3 feature can improve upload performance without requiring the users to change their upload tool significantly?
options: A. S3 Glacier Deep Archive storage class.
B. S3 Transfer Acceleration, which routes uploads through CloudFront edge locations.
C. S3 One Zone-IA.
D. Disabling multipart uploads.

question: An application uses Amazon DynamoDB and is experiencing hot partitions and throttling under heavy write load. The partition key is a low-cardinality attribute (for example status = "active"). What is the MOST effective remediation?
options: A. Redesign the partition key to have higher cardinality (for example include a random suffix, a timestamp component, or a more unique identifier) so that writes are distributed evenly across partitions. Consider write sharding if necessary.
B. Switch to eventually consistent reads.
C. Increase the provisioned write capacity units only.
D. Enable DynamoDB Streams.

question: A company wants to serve both static assets and a dynamic API from the same domain name with low latency worldwide. Which architecture is recommended?
options: A. Amazon S3 static website hosting only.
B. A single EC2 instance in one Region with a public IP.

C. Amazon CloudFront with multiple origins (S3 for static content, API Gateway or ALB for the dynamic API), using cache behaviors to route paths appropriately, and Lambda@Edge or CloudFront Functions if light request manipulation is needed at the edge.
D. Route 53 latency routing to different ALBs without a CDN.

question: A data processing pipeline needs to read a large CSV file stored in S3 and extract only a subset of rows and columns for further processing. Transferring the entire object every time is expensive and slow. Which feature can improve performance and reduce cost?
options: A. Moving the object to Glacier Deep Archive permanently.
B. Downloading the full object and filtering client-side every time.
C. S3 Select (or S3 Glacier Select for archived objects) to retrieve only the required data using SQL-like expressions.
D. Enabling S3 Versioning.

question: An application requires a shared, high-throughput file system that can be accessed concurrently by thousands of EC2 instances for a machine-learning training job. Which storage service is designed for this use case?
options: A. Amazon FSx for Lustre, which is optimized for high-performance computing and can be linked to S3 for long-term storage.
B. Amazon S3 with the AWS SDK only.
C. Amazon EBS gp3 volumes attached to each instance independently.
D. Amazon EFS with the default bursting mode and no performance considerations.

question: An organization observes that their Amazon CloudFront distribution has a low cache hit ratio for dynamic content. What actions can improve the cache hit ratio?
options: A. Use only signed URLs without any caching configuration.
B. Disable caching entirely so that every request goes to the origin.
C. Increase the origin request timeout to the maximum.
D. Review and optimize cache keys (query strings, headers, cookies), set appropriate TTLs via Cache-Control headers or CloudFront cache policies, and consider Origin Shield for multi-Region origins.

C. Amazon Athena only for all Spark jobs.
D. AWS Lambda with 15-minute timeouts for multi-hour Spark jobs.

question: A web application experiences unpredictable traffic spikes that last for only a few minutes. The current Auto Scaling group takes several minutes to launch new instances, so users experience errors during the spike. How can performance during spikes be improved?
options: A. Increase the minimum capacity of the Auto Scaling group permanently to the peak level.
B. Disable Auto Scaling and use a single very large instance.

C. Use a combination of scheduled scaling (if spikes are predictable), target tracking or step scaling policies, and consider warm pools or a serverless front-end (Lambda/API Gateway) for the most spiky components. Also ensure the AMI is optimized for fast boot times.
D. Use only Spot Instances without any On-Demand capacity.

question: An application needs to query large amounts of structured data stored in S3 without managing any infrastructure. Query latency of a few seconds is acceptable. Which service is designed for this?
options: A. Amazon DynamoDB with a scan operation on every query.
B. Amazon RDS with the data loaded into a single large instance.
C. Amazon EC2 with a self-managed database.
D. Amazon Redshift Spectrum or Amazon Athena (serverless SQL queries directly on S3 data).

question: An organization is running a containerized microservices application on Amazon EKS. Some services need to communicate with extremely low latency. Which networking approach is recommended for high performance?
options: A. Expose every pod with a public IP address.
B. Use only ClusterIP services with no consideration of AZ placement.

C. Use the Amazon VPC CNI plugin (or an alternative high-performance CNI), consider AWS App Mesh or Kubernetes native service discovery, and place latency-sensitive pods in the same Availability Zone when possible. For the highest performance, evaluate VPC Lattice or host-mode networking carefully.
D. Route all service-to-service traffic through a public Application Load Balancer.

question: A data lake on S3 is queried frequently by multiple teams using different tools. Some queries scan the same large datasets repeatedly. What can improve performance and reduce cost?
options: A. Move all data to Amazon Glacier.
B. Keep the data in a single large CSV file and scan it every time.

C. Convert data to columnar formats (Parquet/ORC), partition the data by relevant keys (date, region, etc.), use compression, and consider a metadata/catalog layer such as AWS Glue Data Catalog. Caching layers or materialized views in a query engine can also help.
D. Disable all indexing and partitioning.

question: An application uses Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. Under load, some clients experience high latency. The team has already optimized the Lambda code. What additional steps can improve performance?
options: A. Enable API Gateway caching for appropriate GET endpoints, provision concurrency for critical Lambda functions to reduce cold starts, and consider Lambda SnapStart (for Java) or larger memory settings (which also increase CPU).
B. Increase the Lambda timeout to 15 minutes for every function.
C. Disable all caching and force every request to hit Lambda.
D. Replace API Gateway with a single EC2 instance.

question: A company needs a high-performance, fully managed Windows file share that supports SMB and can be accessed from thousands of EC2 instances and on-premises servers. Which service is the best fit?
options: A. Amazon S3 with a Windows NFS gateway.
B. Amazon EBS volumes shared via Windows DFS without a managed service.
C. Amazon FSx for Windows File Server.
D. Amazon EFS (primarily NFS).

question: A real-time analytics dashboard needs to display metrics with a latency of only a few seconds after the events occur. Events are generated at a high rate. Which pipeline is MOST appropriate?
options: A. Ingest events into Amazon Kinesis Data Streams (or Firehose), process them with Kinesis Data Analytics or Lambda, and write aggregated results to a low-latency store such as DynamoDB or ElastiCache for the dashboard to query.
B. Store every event as a separate object in S3 and run Athena queries on every page load.
C. Use Amazon SQS with a visibility timeout of 12 hours.
D. Write events synchronously to an RDS database and query it from the dashboard.

question: An application is experiencing high latency when reading frequently accessed data from Amazon DynamoDB. The table is already provisioned with sufficient capacity. What can further reduce latency?
options: A. Enable DynamoDB Streams and process every read through a Lambda function.
B. Add DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX), an in-memory cache cluster that sits in front of DynamoDB and can reduce read latency to microseconds for cache hits.
C. Decrease the provisioned capacity.
D. Switch all reads to strongly consistent reads.

question: A company wants to reduce the time it takes for large files to be downloaded by users around the world. The files are stored in S3. In addition to CloudFront, which S3 feature can help with the initial upload of those large files from distributed offices?
options: A. S3 Object Lock.
B. S3 Transfer Acceleration.
C. S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval.
D. S3 Inventory.

question: A machine-learning training job needs access to a large dataset stored in S3. The training instances require very high sequential read throughput. Which combination provides the best performance?
options: A. Mount S3 using a user-space file system (s3fs) on each instance.

B. Use Amazon FSx for Lustre linked to the S3 bucket (or Amazon S3 with the high-performance AWS CRT libraries / S3A connector for Spark), and place the compute instances in a cluster placement group with enhanced networking.
C. Use Amazon EFS with the default performance mode.
D. Copy the entire dataset to an EBS volume on one instance and share it via NFS.

question: An Application Load Balancer is used in front of a fleet of EC2 instances. Some requests are long-running (several minutes). The default idle timeout is causing connections to be closed. How can this be addressed?
options: A. Reduce the number of instances so that each handles fewer requests.
B. Switch to a Network Load Balancer which has no idle timeout configuration.
C. Disable the load balancer entirely.
D. Increase the ALB idle timeout setting to a value that accommodates the longest expected request (up to 4000 seconds).

question: An organization is designing a content delivery architecture for software downloads (multi-GB files). They want the highest possible download speeds for users worldwide and the ability to invalidate content quickly when a new version is released. Which combination is recommended?
options: A. AWS Snowball devices shipped to each user.
B. A single S3 bucket in one Region with public access.
C. Amazon CloudFront with an S3 origin, appropriate cache behaviors, and the ability to create invalidations (or use versioned object keys for cache busting).
D. Amazon EBS volumes with snapshots shared publicly.

question: An application needs to perform complex graph queries with millisecond latency on a highly connected dataset. Which purpose-built AWS database service is designed for this workload?
options: A. Amazon RDS for MySQL with recursive CTEs.
B. Amazon Neptune (graph database).
C. Amazon DynamoDB with multiple GSIs and application-side joins.
D. Amazon Redshift.

question: A company runs a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances that process steady, predictable workloads 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. The instances are currently all On-Demand. The finance team has asked for a significant reduction in compute cost without changing the application or the instance types. What should the Solutions Architect recommend?
options: A. Purchase Compute Savings Plans or Standard/Convertible Reserved Instances that match the instance family, Region, and term (1 or 3 years) that best fit the commitment the company is willing to make.
B. Move the workloads to AWS Lambda without any analysis of suitability.
C. Terminate half of the instances and hope the remaining ones can handle the load.
D. Switch all instances to Spot Instances immediately.

question: A data analytics company stores large volumes of log data in Amazon S3. The data is frequently accessed for the first 30 days, occasionally accessed for the next 60 days, and almost never accessed after 90 days, but must be retained for 7 years for compliance. How should the storage be optimized for cost?
options: A. Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration that transitions objects to S3 Standard-IA (or Intelligent-Tiering) after 30 days, to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval or Deep Archive after 90 days, and expires or transitions to a compliant archive after the retention period if appropriate.
B. Move everything to S3 Glacier Deep Archive immediately after upload.
C. Store the data on EBS volumes attached to a single EC2 instance.
D. Keep all objects in S3 Standard for the entire 7 years.

question: A development team has a set of Amazon EC2 instances and RDS databases that are only needed during business hours (Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–6 p.m.). Outside these hours the resources sit idle but continue to incur charges. What is the MOST cost-effective approach?
options: A. Leave all resources running 24/7 on On-Demand pricing.
B. Terminate the instances every evening and recreate them from AMIs every morning manually.
C. Purchase 3-year Reserved Instances for the development environment.

D. Use AWS Instance Scheduler (or a custom Lambda + CloudWatch Events solution) to automatically stop EC2 instances and stop/start RDS instances outside business hours. Consider Aurora Serverless or smaller instance sizes for development.

question: A company has many Amazon EC2 instances of various sizes and families. Some are over-provisioned and rarely use more than 20% of their CPU or memory. Which AWS service provides specific rightsizing recommendations?
options: A. AWS Budgets alone.
B. AWS Cost Explorer with no additional features.
C. Amazon CloudWatch only, without any analysis engine.
D. AWS Compute Optimizer (and Trusted Advisor checks for underutilized resources).

question: An organization is designing a new application that will have highly variable and unpredictable traffic. Sometimes the load is near zero for hours; at other times it spikes dramatically. Which compute approach is likely to be the most cost-effective?
options: A. A single very large EC2 instance running continuously.
B. Dedicated Hosts for the entire application.

C. A combination of AWS Lambda (for event-driven or API workloads) and/or EC2 Auto Scaling with a mix of On-Demand and Spot capacity, or Aurora Serverless / Fargate for appropriate components, so that the company pays mainly for what is actually consumed.
D. A fixed fleet of large Reserved Instances sized for peak load.

question: A company has a large amount of data in S3 Standard that is accessed infrequently and can tolerate a retrieval time of a few hours. Which storage class change will reduce cost the most while still meeting the access requirements?
options: A. Keep the data in S3 Standard and enable versioning.
B. Move the data to Amazon EBS Cold HDD volumes.
C. Transition the data to S3 Standard-IA or S3 One Zone-IA if the data is non-critical and can live in a single AZ.
D. Transition the data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.

question: An organization has multiple AWS accounts. Each account receives its own invoice, and the company is missing out on volume discounts. What should they implement to reduce overall cost?
options: A. Keep the accounts completely separate and negotiate individual discounts.
B. Create an AWS Organization and enable consolidated billing so that usage is aggregated for pricing tiers and Reserved Instance / Savings Plans discounts can be shared (where applicable).
C. Merge all workloads into a single AWS account regardless of security or operational boundaries.
D. Use only the AWS Free Tier for all accounts.

question: A batch processing workload runs for several hours each night and can tolerate interruption. The company wants the lowest possible compute cost. Which EC2 purchasing option should be the primary choice?
options: A. Spot Instances (or Spot Fleet / Auto Scaling with Spot), with a fallback to On-Demand if capacity is unavailable, and a design that can resume or restart interrupted jobs.
B. Dedicated Hosts.
C. On-Demand Instances.
D. Standard Reserved Instances for 3 years.

question: A company is paying a significant amount for data transfer out to the internet from their application. The application serves static and dynamic content to users worldwide. What architectural change is MOST likely to reduce data transfer costs?
options: A. Place Amazon CloudFront in front of the application and S3 origins so that the majority of content is served from edge locations; users closer to the edge reduce origin data transfer, and CloudFront data transfer pricing is often more favorable.
B. Move all EC2 instances to a single Availability Zone.
C. Disable all compression on the application.
D. Use only public IPv4 addresses and avoid IPv6.

question: A development team frequently launches large EC2 instances for short-lived tests and forgets to terminate them. This has resulted in unexpected bills. Which combination of tools can help prevent this?
options: A. Disabling the EC2 service in development accounts.
B. Only manual review of the billing console once a month.

C. AWS Budgets with alerts, AWS Instance Scheduler or automated Lambda functions to stop/terminate idle instances, tagging policies, and optionally Service Control Policies that restrict the instance types that can be launched in non-production accounts.
D. Purchasing Reserved Instances for every possible instance type.

question: A company uses Amazon RDS for a production database that runs 24/7 with a stable load. They are currently using On-Demand pricing. What is the simplest way to reduce the database cost significantly?
options: A. Disable Multi-AZ and automated backups.
B. Move the database to a single EC2 instance running MySQL.
C. Purchase an RDS Reserved Instance (or use Savings Plans where applicable) for the instance class and Region in use.
D. Switch to a much smaller instance class without testing.

question: An application generates a large number of small log files that are written to S3 every few seconds. The company has noticed high request costs (PUT requests). How can the cost of writing the logs be reduced?
options: A. Disable logging entirely.

B. Buffer the log records and write larger objects less frequently (for example using Kinesis Data Firehose with S3 as the destination, or an application-side buffer), and consider using S3 Intelligent-Tiering or lifecycle policies for the resulting objects.
C. Write the logs to an EBS volume instead of S3.
D. Continue writing every small file individually.

question: A company has a large number of Amazon EBS snapshots that are no longer needed. They also have unattached EBS volumes. What actions will reduce storage costs?
options: A. Delete unnecessary snapshots and unattached volumes. Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (DLM) or AWS Backup policies to automate retention going forward. Consider converting gp2 volumes to gp3 for better price/performance.
B. Move all snapshots to S3 Glacier manually without a lifecycle policy.
C. Leave all snapshots and volumes in place indefinitely.
D. Create more frequent snapshots of every volume.

question: A serverless application uses AWS Lambda and Amazon API Gateway. The functions are invoked infrequently but the team has configured provisioned concurrency for all of them at a high level. The bill is higher than expected. What should be reviewed?
options: A. Increase provisioned concurrency further to improve performance.
B. Replace Lambda with always-on EC2 instances.
C. Switch every function to the maximum memory setting.

D. Right-size or remove unnecessary provisioned concurrency; use it only for functions that truly require consistent low latency and have predictable traffic. For spiky or low-traffic functions, on-demand concurrency is usually more cost-effective.

question: A company is using NAT Gateways in every Availability Zone for a large number of private subnets. The data transfer and hourly charges for the NAT Gateways are significant. What are valid cost-optimization strategies?
options: A. Keep a NAT Gateway in every AZ regardless of actual traffic patterns.
B. Replace all NAT Gateways with internet gateways on private subnets.

C. Evaluate whether VPC endpoints (gateway endpoints for S3/DynamoDB, interface endpoints for other services) can eliminate the need for NAT for a large portion of the traffic; consider a shared NAT Gateway design where appropriate; review whether all subnets truly need outbound internet access.
D. Disable all private subnet route tables.

question: An organization wants to track cost by project, environment (dev/test/prod), and business unit. They currently have no consistent tagging strategy. What is the recommended first step?
options: A. Create a separate AWS account for every project without any tagging.
B. Use only the AWS Free Tier and avoid any cost analysis.

C. Define a mandatory tagging policy (for example Project, Environment, Owner, CostCenter), enforce it with AWS Organizations Service Control Policies or IAM policies, activate cost allocation tags in Billing, and use Cost Explorer and Cost and Usage Reports to analyze spend by tag.
D. Ignore tagging and only look at the total bill.

question: A company has a containerized application running on Amazon ECS with the Fargate launch type. The tasks are over-provisioned with CPU and memory. What should the Solutions Architect recommend?
options: A. Move everything back to EC2 without any analysis.
B. Leave the task definitions at their current large sizes.
C. Analyze CloudWatch Container Insights or Container Metrics, right-size the task CPU and memory values, and consider Savings Plans for Fargate or Fargate Spot for interruptible workloads.
D. Switch to the largest possible Fargate configuration for every task.

question: A data warehouse on Amazon Redshift is used heavily during business hours but is almost idle at night and on weekends. How can the company reduce cost while keeping the cluster available when needed?
options: A. Delete the cluster every evening and restore from snapshot every morning.
B. Switch to Amazon Athena for all workloads without evaluating query patterns.
C. Use Redshift’s pause and resume capability (or Elastic Resize / Classic Resize to a smaller size during off-hours), or consider Redshift Serverless if the usage pattern fits.
D. Leave the cluster running at full size 24/7.

question: An organization is transferring large amounts of data from on-premises data centers to Amazon S3. They are currently using the public internet and paying significant egress charges to their ISP as well as experiencing slow transfer rates. Which AWS service can reduce both cost and transfer time for multi-terabyte or petabyte-scale migrations?
options: A. Use AWS DataSync or AWS Snow Family devices (Snowball, Snowball Edge, Snowmobile) depending on the data volume and network bandwidth, or establish an AWS Direct Connect connection for ongoing large transfers.
B. Continue using the public internet with multiple parallel streams only.
C. Email the data on hard drives without any tracking.
D. Use only single-threaded SCP over the internet.

question: An application uses Amazon ElastiCache for Redis. The cache is running on a large node type 24/7, but CloudWatch metrics show that memory utilization is consistently below 30% and CPU is low. What should be done?
options: A. Right-size the node type based on the observed utilization, and consider Reserved Nodes if the cache will run continuously for a year or more.
B. Switch to a multi-AZ configuration with three times the capacity without analysis.
C. Disable the cache entirely.
D. Increase the node type to the next larger size.

question: A company has enabled detailed monitoring (1-minute metrics) for all EC2 instances and has hundreds of custom CloudWatch metrics. The CloudWatch bill is higher than expected. How can costs be reduced without losing essential visibility?
options: A. Keep detailed monitoring and all custom metrics indefinitely.
B. Disable all CloudWatch monitoring.
C. Send every log line as a separate custom metric.

D. Switch non-critical instances to basic monitoring (5-minute metrics), reduce the number of custom metrics, use metric filters and aggregation where possible, and set appropriate retention periods for logs. Evaluate whether Contributor Insights or other advanced features are necessary.

question: An organization is using Amazon S3 for a data lake. They have many small objects (a few KB each), which increases the cost of LIST and GET requests and also affects performance. What optimization can help?
options: A. Keep every record as an individual object.

B. Aggregate small objects into larger objects (for example using file formats such as Parquet with row groups, or simply concatenating files), and use S3 Inventory or S3 Batch Operations for management. Consider S3 Intelligent-Tiering for automatic cost optimization of the resulting objects.
C. Move every small object to Glacier Instant Retrieval.
D. Enable versioning on every object without any lifecycle policy.

question: A company has a three-year commitment window and a very stable EC2 footprint. They want the maximum discount available. Which purchasing option typically provides the highest savings?
options: A. On-Demand Instances.
B. Spot Instances for non-interruptible production workloads.
C. Dedicated Hosts without any reservation.
D. 3-year All Upfront Standard Reserved Instances or the equivalent Compute Savings Plans with a 3-year all-upfront commitment.

question: An application currently runs on a fleet of m5.2xlarge On-Demand instances. After analyzing utilization, the team determines that m5.xlarge instances would be sufficient. They also want to reduce cost further for the steady-state portion of the fleet. What combination of actions is recommended?
options: A. Move the application to the largest available instance type.
B. Keep the m5.2xlarge instances and purchase Reserved Instances for them.
C. Right-size to m5.xlarge (or the appropriate size recommended by Compute Optimizer), then purchase Savings Plans or Reserved Instances for the right-sized instances.
D. Switch everything to Spot Instances without any On-Demand or reserved capacity.

question: A company is using AWS Lambda for a high-volume API. They notice that a large percentage of the cost is from a few functions that process large payloads and run for several seconds. How can they reduce cost?
options: A. Profile the functions, optimize the code and dependencies, right-size the memory setting (because CPU scales with memory), and consider whether some of the work can be moved to asynchronous processing with SQS/SNS or to a container-based service if the workload is more efficient there.
B. Set all functions to the maximum memory of 10 GB.
C. Increase the memory allocation of those functions further (which may or may not help, depending on whether the functions are CPU-bound or memory-bound).
D. Disable the functions during peak hours.

question: A company has a multi-account environment and wants to ensure that developers cannot launch expensive GPU instances in non-production accounts. How can this be enforced centrally?
options: A. Ask developers politely not to launch GPU instances.
B. Use AWS Organizations Service Control Policies (SCPs) to deny the launch of specific instance types (or families) in the non-production organizational units or accounts.
C. Use only CloudWatch Alarms after the instances have been launched.
D. Remove the EC2 service from all non-production accounts.

question: An analytics workload uses Amazon Athena to query data in S3. The queries are scanning far more data than necessary, resulting in high costs. What practices will reduce Athena query costs?
options: A. Store data as large uncompressed CSV files and SELECT * on every query.
B. Increase the number of Athena workers manually for every query.
C. Move all data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive and query it directly with Athena.

D. Convert data to columnar formats (Parquet/ORC), partition the tables by commonly filtered columns, use compression, and avoid SELECT * — only project the columns needed. Consider partitioning and file size optimization (aim for 100 MB–1 GB files).

question: A company is running a production application on EC2 and wants to reduce cost while maintaining the ability to handle unexpected load spikes. Which strategy balances cost and performance?
options: A. Use an Auto Scaling group with a base of Reserved / Savings Plans capacity (or On-Demand) sized for the typical load, and allow the group to scale out using Spot Instances (with diversification across instance types and AZs) for the variable portion of demand. Use a suitable scaling policy.
B. Disable Auto Scaling and manually launch instances when needed.
C. Run only Spot Instances with no On-Demand capacity.
D. Run a fixed number of the largest possible On-Demand instances at all times.

question: An organization has enabled AWS Cost Explorer and is reviewing the “RI/SP Coverage” and “RI/SP Utilization” reports. They notice that a significant portion of their compute usage is still On-Demand even though they have purchased Savings Plans. What should they investigate?
options: A. Nothing — Savings Plans automatically cover every possible usage.

B. Whether the Savings Plans type (Compute vs EC2 Instance), term, payment option, and the actual usage patterns (Region, instance family, etc.) are aligned. They may need additional Savings Plans or to adjust the mix of instance types to better match the existing commitment.
C. Switch everything to Spot Instances only.
D. Cancel all Savings Plans immediately.

question: A company stores infrequently accessed documents in S3 and wants to minimize storage cost while keeping the documents available for retrieval within minutes if needed. Which storage class is the MOST cost-effective choice?
options: A. S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) or S3 One Zone-IA (if the data is recreatable and single-AZ is acceptable).
B. S3 Standard.
C. S3 Express One Zone (high-performance, higher cost).
D. S3 Glacier Deep Archive (retrieval in hours).
